title: Giving Back the Alarm Clock: Who Owns Waking Up
summary: A planned, reversible handoff that helps a teenager own morning preparation while adults retain safety, access and attendance responsibilities.
meta_description: How to transfer the morning routine to a teenager, what a survivable failure looks like, and when to step back in.

core_belief_shift.from: I have to keep waking him or I am careless.
core_belief_shift.to: I can transfer morning responsibility through a planned, reversible handoff while retaining adult duties for safety and access.

release_move: Alarm Handoff: launch an explicit agreement, log outcomes, repair the system after a miss, then re-release after a short scaffold.

book_relevance.reason: No Playbook is the useful next tool; this guide needs a practical family handoff.

hero.alt: A teenage boy checks his own morning alarm and school bag while his mother calmly prepares breakfast nearby.

social_image.alt: A teenage boy checks his own morning alarm and school bag while his mother calmly prepares breakfast nearby.
